public_rationale: Alexa+ is substantial evidence against treating the capability as indefinitely remote: Amazon reports tens of millions of participants, and independent testing demonstrates conversation and useful home control. But the records do not establish reliability across millions of homes. More fundamentally, Marcus supplied no deadline, so assigning a failure after an evaluator-chosen number of years would add a commitment he did not make. No conclusive event satisfies the stated rule.
limitations: One household’s successes and defects cannot establish population-wide reliability.
Even a verified milestone date would leave the meaning of long, long way away disputed.

our_interpretation: The milestone requires an operational LLM-based conversational assistant with home-control capability and evidence of practical reliability at household scale.
Millions means at least two million homes. Customer accounts, supported devices, and availability are not automatically counts of homes using the product.
Reliable enough means dependable ordinary home-control use, not perfection.
Long, long way away supplies no defensible calendar deadline. I do not substitute a fixed number of years.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently distant arrival date for a product meeting all stated requirements could support the forecast, but the speaker supplies no duration that can be scored mechanically.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented arrival shortly after the post, meeting conversation, home control, household scale, and practical reliability requirements, would contradict an unambiguously distant-arrival reading.
